chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Fats misses him and pouts like a child
summary: While he was out with Hopkins, a Chicago hotel booking came for Fats, who demanded Hermie and sulked like a kid whose toy was taken.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: So, I went with Claud to do a few dates, and while we were out the singer, Claud Hopkins' singer, hm, hm, hm, hm hm, hm, thin man.

Orlando Robertson. Came back and as the people heard, he was back with Claud (snap, snap, snap) Claud's offers start -- got swamped with -- we want Claud. We want Claud and Orlando, mainly, since he was back.

So some more dates come in, and instead of us coming back to New York, and Claud say I got two or three more dates, can you make them? I said well, yes, I guess so, you know. And since I hadn't heard anything, I said two or three more dates are not going to hurt. And one -- this particular date took us to West Virginia, and Fats' booking came in, because the thing in Chicago, the hotel in Chicago had the room. He didn't mention it to me, and that -- now that's where Fats was like a kid. He would get very mad, should he say well, call Wilson and tell him I want -- he'd say why? What do you mean, he's not here? Get him!
You'd say well, he left town. He left town.
he'd hit the ceiling, you know? And he's mad. He's
like a kid when you steal his favorite toy, or something. You know, he'd pout like a bastard. See?
When they -- all the same time, say go ahead, you know, so he don't appreciate me, see? You go away (smack) leave me all by myself. I need him. He's not here.
